_comment: Wall-clock seconds for one bats file in its own bats call on a GitHub windows-latest runner, Node 20. Used ONLY to balance CI shards -- never to gate anything. Stale numbers cost balance, never correctness: shard-tests.mjs asserts every file lands in exactly one shard whether or not it appears here.
_why: arc-ci's windows leg costs 1585s against ~145s on ubuntu for the same 563 tests -- 2.82s per test against 0.26s, because every bats `run` spawns a process and windows process creation is dear. Measured 2026-07-31 (run 30611012771): excluding the workspace and bats' binaries from Microsoft Defender changes nothing, because the runner image already ships with realtime protection OFF and both drives excluded. There is no windows-side saving left to find, so the fix stays splitting.
_provenance: Every one of the 104 files re-measured in a single pass on 2026-08-10 (run 31361908896, weigh-tests.yml, on feat/arc-leads-slice-06-fixes) -- one file per job, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs. Re-run that workflow and paste its block rather than editing numbers by hand: a hand-picked weight is a guess wearing a measurement. METHOD FOR memory-index.bats, which differs from the weigh-tests.yml pass and says so: weigh-tests.yml takes no inputs and weighs all 105 files one job each, which is far too heavy to dispatch once per phase. The ordinary arc-ci log is timestamped per TAP line and the file runs inside ONE bats call in its shard, so the span from the TAP line before its first test to its last IS its contribution to that shard -- which is exactly what the weight represents. Measured on windows, because this table is windows seconds by construction. 31 tests, 44.5s. Re-measure it in the next full weigh-tests pass rather than trusting this number forever: it is a real measurement of a real run, but it was taken alongside other files rather than in isolation. memory-recall.bats was measured the same way on 2026-08-11 (run 31489671716, windows shard 10/12): 26 tests, 59.9s, entered as 60. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-11 after Phase 02 REQ-04 grew it to 31 tests (run 31527262396, windows shard 7/12, span ok-68 19:24:31.432 -> ok-99 19:25:51.742): 31 tests, 80.3s, entered as 80. A weight is re-measured whenever its file GROWS, not only when a full weigh pass is dispatched -- five tests moved this file 20s, which is more than a third of its old weight and enough to unbalance a shard on its own. memory-conflict.bats was measured the same way at birth in the same run (windows shard 11/12, span ok-189 19:26:06.475 -> ok-199 19:26:27.592): 10 tests, 21.1s, entered as 21, so it never rode _default_weight 16 unmeasured for even one run. memory-golden.bats likewise, measured at birth in run 31533461767 (windows shard 12/12, span ok-207 20:39:45.748 -> ok-217 20:40:11.016): 10 tests, 25.3s, entered as 25. Three memory files have now been weighed by this per-file TAP-span method rather than by a weigh-tests dispatch; it is a real measurement of a real run taken alongside other files, so re-measure all three in the next full pass rather than trusting them forever. memory-hook.bats measured the same way at birth in run 31539062289 (windows shard 4/12, span ok-174 21:47:31.367 -> ok-183 21:47:45.301): 9 tests, 13.9s, entered as 14. Four memory files are now weighed by this per-file TAP-span method; re-measure all four in the next full weigh-tests pass. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-12 after the 21 open adversarial findings were closed, each with a test: run 31573674899 (head 95ed6e1, 19/19 green), same per-file TAP-span method, windows legs. memory-recall 31->33 tests, shard 9/12, 93.5s, entered as 94 (was 80). memory-golden 14->19 tests, shard 10/12, 45.8s, entered as 46 (was 25). memory-hook 9->11 tests, shard 5/12, 32.1s, entered as 32 (was 14). memory-conflict 10->11 tests, shard 2/12, 22.1s, entered as 22 (was 21). Every one of the four GREW, and three of the four moved by more than their own old weight in absolute terms -- memory-golden nearly doubled -- which is exactly the case the grow-then-re-measure rule exists for: carrying the old numbers would have under-weighted one shard by 84s. All four are still per-file TAP spans taken alongside other files rather than a weigh-tests dispatch; re-measure all four in the next full pass.
_evidence: The 2026-08-10 pass measured 104 files, 44 of which had NO entry at all and were riding _default_weight 16. The two this slice grew were among them and wrong in the same direction by roughly sevenfold: leads-journey.bats 111s and leads-mail-guard.bats 120s. (An earlier version of this sentence said 47 covered; 47 was the count MISSING before the run, 44 of them were measured, and the other 3 are the ones _known_gap names.) The method is unchanged from the pass that produced the previous table: one file per job on windows, each timed in its own bats call with the scanners arc-ci installs.
_floor: spine-emit.bats at 160s is the floor no shard count can beat, and design-steel-thread.bats at 156s is second. Both numbers are from the 2026-08-10 pass; the previous prose here quoted 147s and 128s from the 2026-08-03 pass and was left standing when the table under it was replaced -- a measured claim that stops being re-derived starts lying, which is the whole reason this file records provenance. From 12 shards on, the heaviest shard IS that one file, and one file cannot be split.
_known_gap: UNMEASURED, AND COUNTED SO THE GAP IS VISIBLE RATHER THAN DEFAULTED: 3 file(s) -- absorb-ab-run.bats, absorb-rebuild-t01.bats, spine-worktree-guard.bats -- ride _default_weight 16. memory-index.bats is no longer among them: it was named here the moment it landed and MEASURED at 44s from run 31484005819, windows shard 10/12, before Phase 00 closed. They arrived with the origin/main merge AFTER this weigh run was dispatched, so they are genuinely unmeasured rather than overlooked. lanes.md: a missing entry is a default rather than an error, so the count is stated here. These are WINDOWS seconds and the macOS leg is sharded with them, which is wrong in kind: the last 2-shard macOS split came out 77s and 161s against a prediction of 797/796, because the process-spawn cost that dominates windows does not dominate macOS. macOS is given a third shard to make the error small rather than a weights table of its own, since at 238s total it is not the binding leg. If it ever becomes one, weigh it on macos-latest instead of tuning the shard count.
